priceSnapshot.note: The morning breakout failed and the eighteen-session floor broke with it. Since the morning snapshot at 64,397.6 price made one more push to 64,500.0 - clearing the session high and tagging the 15m EMA200 - and then reversed for 1,050 points to 63,450.0, ending 811.3 points below where the morning session marked, a -1.26% move in under six hours. The reversal was not drift. Three consecutive hourly bars did the damage: 13:00Z closed 64,204.7, 14:00Z closed 63,770.1 after trading down to 63,700.0, and 15:00Z closed 63,606.0 after a 419.9-point range. The single most important fact in this report is that 63,750 finally gave way on a CLOSE. The desk has published that reduce line for eighteen consecutive sessions and it survived five separate wick approaches - 63,832.3, 63,818.1, 63,859.3, 63,913.3 and 63,700.0 - without a settled hourly close beneath 63,892.9. Today two hourly bars settled under it back to back, 63,606.0 at 15:00Z and 63,511.9 at 16:00Z. That is the reduce trigger firing exactly as it was written, and it dragged price through the 4H EMA200 at 63,758.88 on the way. There is a real catalyst behind it: Trump's demand for fifty years of compensation from Iran killed the Strait-of-Hormuz reopening narrative that drove the overnight rally, and Brent has round-tripped from 87.64 at the morning read to 88.73 now, +1.15% on the day. Strategy also disclosed a further sale of its bitcoin holdings. The counterweight is location: spot at 63,586.3 is sitting 86.3 points above a $1,598,958 realized-liquidation shelf at 63,500 - the largest cluster on the tape - with the 1H RSI at 30.05 and the 15m RSI at 31.32. This is a confirmed break into an oversold reading directly on top of the biggest magnet on the map, which is the worst possible place to chase.

reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE below $63,400. NEW LEVEL - the old 63,750 line fired this session and is now spent, so the reduce line steps down to the next structural shelf. 63,400 sits 50.0 points beneath the session low of 63,450.0 and is anchored on a $669,863 realized long-liquidation cluster at the 63,400 handle. Its significance is what lies immediately above it: the $1,598,958 shelf at 63,500, the single largest cluster on the 24-hour tape and only 86.3 points below spot. A settled hourly close under 63,400 means that magnet was consumed rather than defended, which removes the last shelf of any size before the 63,000 handle - and with the 4H EMA200 at 63,758.88 now overhead rather than underneath, there is no moving average between here and there to slow it.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE back above $63,800, WITH open interest FALLING across the same bar. Both halves are new. The price half is a reclaim of the 4H EMA200 at 63,758.88 plus the $1,364,443 long-liquidation shelf at 63,800, which together are what price lost on the way down - taking them back on a close would make today's break a failed breakdown rather than a trend change. The open-interest half is INVERTED from the test this desk has run for the last nine sessions, and the inversion is deliberate. Open interest is 2,137,066,952 against the morning read of 2,082,197,596, UP 2.64%, which means fresh leverage was added into a 811-point decline - those are new shorts, not new longs. A reclaim of 63,800 while that open interest stays high would just be a bounce into supply; a reclaim while open interest falls is those shorts covering, which is the only version worth buying.

decisionBox.changed: This is the largest single-session stance change in the file. Bias moves from range with a bullish tilt to outright bearish, and confidence rises from 5.75 to 6.25 - higher conviction in a worse outcome, because a signal that fires cleanly is more informative than one that hovers. Four things flipped. The 63,750 reduce line fired on two consecutive settled hourly closes after surviving eighteen sessions. Price lost the 4H EMA200 at 63,758.88, the last structural floor. The daily MACD histogram, which this desk has repeatedly called its most reliable slow signal, rolled from +42.83 to -7.10 and is now negative for the first time in the current stretch. And the liquidation flow reversed again: the short-covering squeeze the morning session identified exhausted itself at 64,500 and long liquidations resumed. What did NOT change: the long/short account ratio is still 1.68, and yesterday's -$144.6m ETF outflow is still the most recent completed print. The decision box moves from ADD to REDUCE and the wallet acts on it.

calibration.rollingRecord: The desk has now published a reduce level for eighteen consecutive sessions. It has fired twice: at 64,650 on 10 August morning, honoured the same session, and at 63,750 TODAY at midday. The 63,750 line survived five separate approaches across five sessions - lows of 63,832.3, 63,818.1, 63,859.3, 63,913.3 and 63,700.0 - before settling two consecutive hourly closes beneath it at 63,606.0 and 63,511.9. That is a level that did its job: it held through five false alarms and then broke on the sixth with a real catalyst behind it, which is exactly the behaviour a well-placed line should show. The 64,650 add trigger has now not fired for ten consecutive sessions and its open-interest confirmation clause has blocked ten would-be entries; the morning session declined to open leverage specifically because open interest was flat rather than rising, and price then fell 811 points, so that clause has now saved the desk from a leveraged long twice in two days.
calibration.note: priorReduceFired is TRUE for only the second time in the file's history. The morning session published a reduce line at 63,750 requiring a settled 1H close beneath it; the 15:00Z bar closed 63,606.0 and the 16:00Z bar closed 63,511.9. The signal fired as written and this session acts on it. actingHelped is FALSE and the accounting is unflattering. The morning session moved the decision box to ADD and deployed 12 USDT of spot at 64,397.6 on the argument that price had reclaimed the daily EMA20, the 1H MACD histogram had turned positive, and the liquidation tape had flipped to punishing shorts. All three observations were true and all three reversed within six hours; that tranche is now -1.26%. The midnight tranche of 20 USDT at 63,982.5 is -0.62%. Two things are worth recording against the desk's own reasoning. FIRST, the morning report explicitly identified the risk and sized for it - it wrote that price sitting ON the 1H EMA200 at a triple confluence was 'the worst place to commit the last ammunition', deployed 12 rather than the available 35.53, and named a rejection at that EMA200 as 'the single most likely way this session gives the overnight move back'. That is exactly what happened. The partial sizing was correct even though the direction was wrong, and it is the reason the damage is 1.26% on 12 USDT rather than on 35.53. Partial sizing under mixed evidence is now 3 for 3 as a risk decision even though it is 2 for 3 on direction. SECOND, and less comfortably: the morning session had the bearish evidence in hand and discounted it. The 4H MACD histogram at -120.76 was described as 'the clearest negative in the whole report' and the report still moved to ADD on faster-timeframe signals. The lesson being written to the ledger is that a 4H structure that has 'stopped deteriorating' is not the same as one that has repaired, and the slower timeframe deserved the heavier weight.
